evidence.observation: H701 reads 433.8 °C while H702 and the reboiler vessel read 70.6 and 70.4 °C, respectively.
H701 has risen to 442.7 °C while H702 is 73.3 °C and the vessel is 72.1 °C; the persistent extreme discrepancy indicates possible heater overheating or a temperature-measurement fault.
Cooling-water flow reads zero throughout all 21 events despite the elevated heater temperature.
Distillate flow is 0.7 and reflux flow is zero; earlier flows were mostly zero with intermittent small readings.
System pressure is 499.6 mbar and differential pressures are 0.6 and 2.8 mbar; pressures have remained approximately stable, without identifying the cause of the thermal/cooling anomaly.

args.missing_evidence: Independent H701 temperature verification, heater setpoints/power and safety limits, and physical confirmation of cooling-water circulation are needed to distinguish actual overheating or cooling failure from faulty instrumentation. No composition measurement or separation target has been provided.
